Extreme pastosity would indicate that the writer’s tastes are physical and sensual. They would affect him so much that he could not control his reactions. There would be blurred moral judgment. Absence of these indicators means that these conditions do not exist.

indikator.nama: Initial strokes without arcades and without initial hooks
indikator.keterangan:
With initial strokes arcaded, the writer would be defensive, inhibited and fearful. He would refuse to reveal his innermost self, and he would be very reticent about matters of a personal nature. He would shun emotional contacts. He would adapt to his environment for self-protective reasons.

With frequent initial hooks the writer would be insecure. Because of unfulfilled emotional needs he would seek people and things that offer security. He would be possessive of people and covetous of material things. Lack of these indicators proves absence of these characteristics.

Elaborations would be evidence of insecurity and conflicts within the writer. They would reveal defensiveness and caution. With elaborations, the writer may try to conceal certain personal problems, lie or evade the truth. He may exaggerate, have a distorted view of himself or lack a sense of reality.
Absence of this indicator confirms absence of these problems.

indikator.nama: Ovals clear (all ovals must be clear, no exceptions)
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-3 on page 68.
See listing 13-2 on page 83.

indikator.nama: Soldered strokes none — writing is entirely free of soldered strokes
indikator.keterangan: Soldered strokes would mean that the writer is basically very anxious and uneasy. His basic attitude is one of fear that someone will see through him and uncover the inner conflicts he refuses to admit to himself. As a result, he constantly tries to manipulate the impression he makes on the outside. Lack of this indicator means absence of this characteristic.
See listing 05-4 on page 29.
See listing 05-8a on page 31.
See listing 06-9 on page 42.
See listing 11-6 on page 69.
See listing 11-8 on page 70.

indikator.nama: Score for Mental Orientation (#7) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer sets high standards for himself and has feelings of obligations toward others.

indikator.nama: Score for Self-control (#15) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer exercises conscious control over himself, his emotions, desires and needs. He considers consequences before going into action and he rarely responds before he has taken the time to think.

indikator.nama: Score for Manipulative (#28) is 3.5 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is willing to establish close and constructive relations with others. He is sensitive to others’ needs and handles everyday situations, including his own emotional upsets, without resorting to inappropriate behavior.

indikator.nama: Score for Passive-Dependent (#31) is 3.5 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer takes responsibility for his own life and for the fulfillment of his needs. He does not expect others to solve his difficulties. He appreciates people who share his belief in the importance of each person doing his or her thing.

indikator.nama: Score for Withdrawal (#32) is 3.5 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer feels emotionally secure and is willing to engage in open and honest relationships with others. He enjoys being familiar with others and makes others feel at ease, too.

indikator.nama: Score for Suspicious (#33) is 3.5 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is inclined to believe in others. He is willing to give them his trust, unless they actually prove themselves to be unworthy.

indikator.nama: Score for Pessimism (#34) is 3.5 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer generally feels good about people and circumstances. He is optimistic about himself and other people and is often an inspiration to others.
See listing 08-1a on page 52.
See listing 01-1 on page 3.

With arcades more frequent than required by copybook, the writer lacks spontaneity. He is controlled, reserved and secretive. He has a natural sense of what can threaten his security. He closes himself off and responds to new people and situations with caution. He is unwilling to openly display feelings, either of sorrow or joy and he is reticent about himself and his most personal thoughts. He is likewise unreceptive to familiar overtures from others. When he seeks contact, it is usually for ulterior reasons. He is motivated by caution, calculation and fear of possible consequences.

The writer derives security from tradition and origin. He stays with what is traditional and considered well-accepted behavior by society. Appearance in behavior and in the moral sense is very important to him. He derives a sense of self worth from knowing that he adheres to principles which he considers valuable and which others respect. He submits to conventional ways of thinking because he is afraid to set himself apart. He is unoriginal in most of his opinions and thoughts. He follows the concepts established by family, teachers and, most importantly, his reference group. He finds that following a pattern of conformity is safer than observing his own independent beliefs. He seeks approval for what he does and for conforming to others' expectations. He follows the customs of his peer group due to fear of being thought of as unconventional.

The writer takes risks carefully and prefers traditional methods of getting ahead. He is bound to the familiar and distrustful of new ideas. He clings to known methods and “safe” procedures and works best where no independent thinking is required. His approach seldom varies since it has been proven effective in the past. He can be depended upon to follow instructions in areas which he already knows. He is overwhelmed when faced with challenges larger than he is accustomed to. He is most comfortable when he can “ease” into a new situation. If he should get involved in unfamiliar activities, either by being chosen, or through circumstances beyond his control, he feels extremely threatened and tense.

The writer is dependent and predictable. He is uneasy when he violates standards of behavior and becomes upset when others disregard established rules. Contradictory behavior in others is hard for him to accept. He becomes indignant, even intolerant, when he sees violations of the rules he, himself, obeys.

Vocationally, the writer is most satisfied in a conserving kind of job, such as the healing arts, museum keeper, repair mechanic, antique dealer, dentist, domestic help, and all kinds of maintenance jobs.

The writer is constricting his movement as well as slowing it down to make the exact placement. This demonstrates insecurity which must be verified through additional indicators.

The writer is insecure. He exercises strict controls to avoid errors for fear of leaving himself open to criticism. He limits himself to the well-known, the familiar, and to things he had success with in the past. He has a careful outlook and restricts himself in his ambitions, his interpersonal relationships and in his work.

The writer is very concerned with detail s. In his daily life, particulars are his main concern. When he is presented with a job, he breaks it down immediately into the parts which form it. Then he starts to work on them, one at a time. He habitually narrows his focus down until the detail becomes the project. For him, details often loom out of proportion to their usefulness or worth. He wastes time and emotion on them. He becomes upset when even the most petty or unimportant items are not taken care of. Even important projects will be interrupted repeatedly to take care of particulars and the writer becomes upset with those who don't take care of trivia the way he does.

He rarely completes a project to his own satisfaction because there are always some loose ends yet to be taken care of. He approaches jobs from the part, not from the whole. If one aspect of an assignment is not completed according to his standards, his appreciation for the whole project is spoiled. Each small item looms out of proportion and causes an inner feeling of apprehension. Until the writer removes the cause of his upset by taking care of the detail, he cannot focus his attention back on the big job. He becomes very upset when deadlines, appointments and commitments are not met exactly on time. He wants accuracy and he wants it now. On the positive side, he functions well around machinery because he tends to handle equipment with a great amount of attention and care.

These writers are self-disciplined and unable to relax. Their predominant characteristics are severity, coldness, austerity and the inability to enjoy sensual pleasures. Fundamentally, they are aesthetically or intellectually oriented. They withdraw from the material world and habitually shun emotional involvements.

These writers make clear moral distinctions and see things as either black or white without middle ground and find it hard, if not impossible, to compromise. Once they have mentally committed themselves, it is difficult for them to reverse their position. They are unrelenting toward their own weaknesses and endure despite discouragement. They apply harsh self-discipline and do not allow themselves to relax. Often, they are trying to give their excessive severity the guise of virtue. These individuals are by nature refined in character, manner and speech. They abhor vulgarity and become upset by any sign of coarseness in their environment.

These writers are extremely critical and see the flaw in almost anything immediately. Vocationally, they fit best into jobs requiring sharp distinctions and observance of precise tolerances. They would perform well as lawyers, surgeons, or critics. They could also be skilled master mechanics.

The writer has to apply conscious controls to stay with a task, even for only a short period of time. Whatever willpower he applies is done by conscious effort.
By nature, he has a low level of energy. His small storehouse of strength has been overtaxed and his energy resources are exhausted. He has no endurance or stamina left. He is incapable of hard work or prolonged effort. Whatever he does, he does under strain. Lack of energy affects every area of his life. It is difficult for him to remain confident. He tends to feel negative for no reason and deems life a trial, rather than an opportunity. He feels weighed down by things he does not like but feels helpless to do anything about it. He suffers from constant anxiety without a specific reason. He is frightened of the risks, uncertainties and dangers of life. He lacks the vitality for emotional experiences. He needs extra large amounts of sleep and often uses it as an escape. As a protection for his delicate nature, the writer tries to avoid anything that does not appear absolutely hygienic or clean.With a sharp ductus, the writer is thin-skinned and hypersensitive.
(Very light pressure may be an early indicator of impending poor health.)
See listing 05-4 on page 29.

Even people close to the writer rarely know what goes on inside of him. He exercises strict controls to keep his emotional reactions hidden. He finds it difficult to express his emotional needs and does not allow others to know about them. He finds it hard to accept from those around him, either suggestions, praise, emotional feelings, or material things. He finds it equally difficult to give of himself or to tune in to others’ emotional requirements. Insecurity makes him shut out other people's views. He stays with that which is familiar. He is loyal due to fear of changing. A side effect is that he restricts his potential.

One area where he may behave in a more relaxed way is in his job where he can deal with people intellectually. He is also more at ease in thoroughly familiar surroundings or with people where he knows what to expect. To a degree, he can then be more spontaneous himself.

The right margin is the hardest to regulate. A certain amount of irregularity is to be expected due to the variable length of words.
The writer is over-controlled, defensive and self-protective. He feels the need to rely on a system to keep himself in line. He will do certain things in certain ways. Once he has set up his routine, he has great difficulty adjusting his schedule to changes as he goes along. The effort to do everything by method slows him down in unfamiliar situations. On the other hand, it protects him from becoming involved in challenges which would tax his abilities.
The writer is distrustful of himself and others. He constantly worries over how others will view him. He is careful in how he reacts or how much he displays of his feelings. He fears getting hurt when he exposes his emotions. People could try to manipulate him or take advantage of him.
See listing 05-8a on page 31.

indikator.nama: Slant in middle and upper zone left
indikator.keterangan:
The writer rigidly controls his emotional expression. Most of the time, he is introverted and restrained. He has a natural aversion to expressed emotion and distrusts people who are too demonstrative. He has learned early in life to keep his joys as well as his suffering to himself. Control has come to mean more to him than sharing a relationship.

There is only one group of people he can be comfortable with, and these people are as unresponsive as he is. But when he is with them, he still cannot express what means the most to him, because that would mean abandoning the control he has built up so carefully over the years.

He is unable to respond spontaneously to mental stimuli. He is defensive and self-protective due to fear of disclosing his vulnerabilities. He is suspicious of others’ motives and reacts with much skepticism to others’ ideas and thoughts.

Any job that demands restraint of emotion profits by persons who are unresponsive. Surgeons, executioners, professional gamblers, bill collectors, traffic enforcers, are examples of such professions.

indikator.nama: Slant in middle and upper zone vertical
indikator.keterangan:
The writer controls emotional display by will. Unless an emotion is really intense, very little is likely to show on the surface. Instead he is noncommittal, unemotional and undemonstrative. He is just as controlled in expressing love, affection, and compassion, as he will be in expressing more negative feelings. He does not burden others with his personal pain or problems. Even when he wants to make contact, it is not easy for him to reach out and really communicate with others. When his feelings surface, they are significant. What is being expressed has much meaning since it is so rare. He is self-sufficient as far as the outside world is concerned.

The writer takes an objective view of situations and people. He is observant of his surroundings and other individuals. In his thinking, he is impartial and lacks sentimentality. He is levelheaded and poised. In most situations, he exercises conscious control which uses part of his mental energy to maintain.

The writer functions best where emotional display is not the rule, and he sets for others an example of moderation. He thinks of his controlled behavior as a benefit and an accomplishment. He feels he is more in control of himself and he appreciates similar restraint in others.

indikator.nama: t-bar length short and t-bars carefully placed
indikator.keterangan:
With t-bar length short, the writer is careful not to intrude on the rights of others. He exercises conscious controls in pursuing his goals. He does not want to infringe on the prerogative of his group, family or people he wants to belong to. He will not apply more mental force than he can without risking the feeling of security he has from knowing that what he does is acceptable to the group.

With t-bars carefully placed, the writer is careful and precise due to insecurity.

The writer is adaptable and behaves in such a way that he fits in with the group and others’ expectations. He is outer-directed and susceptible to being influenced by circumstances and other people. That means that others can enthuse him, or discourage him, at least temporarily.

The writer is more responsive to emotional than to logical appeals. He may commit himself before thoroughly considering all consequences.

Careful, long-range planning is difficult. The writer may need encouragement to stay with a long-lasting or troublesome project.

Important! Variable line alignment may be indicative of the ambivalence of hope and fear subsequent to a grievous loss (through death, for instance); in such a case, it will be temporary.

This interpretation does not apply to looped, hanging or supported garlands. It does not pertain to secondary thread.

The writer follows the path of least resistance. He is willing to adapt or compromise in order to expedite things.

With fast writing, the writer has a keen intellect. He is very much aware of what happens around him and responds quickly and spontaneously to people and situations. He is clever and opportunistic and well aware of all the implications of a situation or relationship. He prefers subtlety and suggestions over directness in communication.

The writer has a multitude of interests. He effortlessly performs tasks he has thoroughly learned. Most of the time, he is impatient about getting projects done.

indikator.nama: Connective forms variable (at least 3 out of 5 connective forms)
indikator.keterangan:
The writer is flexible in his interaction with others. He is resourceful and able to work efficiently. He meets changes in his work and surroundings with appropriate behavior and with the confidence that he can cope, even thrive.

The writer is adept at problem solving. He searches out alternative methods when traditional ones no longer work.

indikator.nama: Final strokes fading in slow writing
indikator.keterangan:
With fast writing, finals are supposed to be brief and fade out. Fading finals confirm speed.

With slow writing, the writer fears the finality of a hard and fast decision. Unsure of his judgment, he vacillates, procrastinates, or in other ways hesitates to decide. Afraid of the consequences, he does not want to make unjust or unpopular decisions and he does not wish to commit himself to agreeing or disagreeing. Especially in unfamiliar areas will he be cautious and hesitant.

Decisions that could be made speedily may be delayed pending the development of more and more data, most of which frequently reconfirms what the writer already knows.

As a supervisor, insecurity may so immobilize the writer that he is prevented not only from making decisions himself but also from delegating them, afraid that mistakes made by subordinates will reflect on him.

The writer finds a sort of negative security in temporizing. Refusing to take a stand, he goes back and forth and tends to change his mind frequently. Or he may procrastinate and wait until the time for the decision is past.

The writer is adaptable in the sense that he finds it difficult to commit himself to a feeling or opinion about a situation or another person. His instinctive inclination is to wait for someone else to tell him what to do. He often spends so long weighing each side that the decision is usually made by default or by the other persons involved.

Afraid to rely on his own judgment, he lets others make the choices he should make for and by himself. He waits to see what people want before airing his position and quickly accedes if he thinks someone else knows better (which is most of the time).

Indecisiveness is a handicap because it delays action and wastes time. Instead of making definite decisions and acting on them, the writer tries to keep too many options open. He may even alter plans because of doubts after work has commenced.

The writer is spontaneous, congenial and adaptable. He is compassionate and benevolent and willing to engage himself for the sake of others. He shows emotional generosity. He spontaneously commits his time and energy to those with whom he sympathizes. He has an instinctive tendency to help automatically when he sees a need. He seeks contact and typically possesses good social skills.

Important! When the garland ends in a hook, the writer hides selfish motives behind the generosity.

The writer reaches out toward other people. He is adaptable and has an open mind for new concepts and things. He will consider new ideas sooner than most people and is oriented toward projects which connect him with the future. He wants to establish contact with others and understand his fellow beings.
See listing 03-2 on page 16.
See listing 03-6 on page 18.
See listing 09-5b on page 58.

indikator.nama: Right tendency in the middle zone
indikator.keterangan: See listing 08-7b on page 54.

The writer has a yielding and compliant attitude. He tends to accept the dominion of others and is submissive to his environment. He yields to the command or leadership of other people and rarely takes a definite stand. He is uncommitted and prone to changing his mind. He is indefinite with his words and undetermined about his follow-through. He “sits on the fence,” so to speak, leaving every option open. He quickly accedes if he thinks someone else knows better (which is most of the time) and is willing to let others have their way.

The writer’s conduct and tone of voice make others think of him as weak. He is timid in the way he speaks and his statements sound like questions. He is afraid to stand up for what he believes. Unconsciously, he provokes others to take advantage of him. He is quickly recognized as an individual who will “give in.” Considered an easy pushover, he may often be victimized. He becomes the target because his demeanor reveals how weak he basically is.

The writer is ineffectual in positions requiring command because he fails to follow through with action and he depends upon others for the decisions he should make for himself. He changes course at the slightest suggestion and may compromise himself by his lack of mental commitment.

The writer has to be careful about that in which he becomes involved, especially regarding fidelity in relationships. When committing himself to something, he is wise to pledge in front of many people, sign a contract, or make some kind of down payment, so that he is less likely to turn his back on it later for something which seems more attractive to him.

When somebody betrays him, he may just shrug his shoulders and think, “Good riddance,” and have his eye already on somebody else as an alternative.

He will find it easier to stay with a project if he takes it in smaller segments. It is to his advantage to set modest goals and carry through, rather than to plan an all-out accomplishment and fail.

With acquisitiveness, the writer may be tempted to obtain items he does not need or cannot afford. He may fall prey to fast talking sales people.
See listing 05-8b on page 31.
See listing 06-2a on page 36.
See listing 06-2c on page 36.

indikator.nama: Initial flourishes on H’s, M’s or N’s
indikator.keterangan:
The writer takes serious matters more lightly and is able to see the funny side of life. He often sees humor in places where many are too insensitive to notice. He likely appreciates witty remarks and amusing commentaries.

His sense of humor often adds a touch of fun to what he is doing. It also prevents him from taking himself too seriously. He can chuckle at what is funny in himself without loss of self-esteem. He can make light of his shortcomings and laugh even when the joke is on himself.

Often a spark of humor comes to his aid in strained situations and helps to release tension in a positive and uplifting way. Laughing with others creates a bond of understanding. It gives others the feeling of being included because laughter is always with them, never at their expense.

With a touch of humor adjustment is usually easier for him.
See listing 16-5a on page 99.
See listing 16-5b on page 99.
See listing 05-4 on page 29.
See listing 05-1 on page 28.

The writer is emotionally accessible and freely communicates his feelings to others. This refers as well to warm appreciative sensations as to feelings of discomfort, distress, concern and fear. The more profound the inner response, the stronger the outward display. He is more generous in responding to the emotional needs of others, too, and more attuned to the sensations around him. He is warm, friendly and understanding. His response is genuine and not impulsive. He moves freely outward, becomes involved and allows others to get to know him. He is willing to risk rejection by demonstrating his feelings.

The writer is receptive to the thoughts of others and open to new ideas. Unfamiliar concepts do not frighten him. He shares his views and invites others to express theirs, too.

He is organized and orderly and learns and works without feelings of distraction.

The writer is emotionally responsive to people. He is able to express his feelings spontaneously and appropriately. He is communicative and sympathetic in understanding others’ emotional needs. He is friendly, sociable and willing to become involved. He allows others to get to know him, as long as they don’t get too personal which would arouse anxiety.

The writer is receptive to the ideas of other people. He is able to learn from them. He is adaptable in responding to their behavior and working methods. Assurance helps him to move forward and be progressive.

This includes the signature.
Self-protective strokes would show that the writer does not feel good about himself and that he feels the need to cover himself. He would assume that others are criticizing or belittling him. This would affect communication negatively. Lack of this indicator means absence of this trait.

Cover strokes would reveal severe emotional inhibitions. There would be self-protective tendencies leading to feelings of guilt, despondency, evasiveness, self-deception and deceit. Lack of cover strokes verifies absence of these characteristics.

indikator.nama: Letter height decreasing toward end of word
indikator.keterangan: The writer has a special skill in handling people. He is gracious, courteous and diplomatic. He is more tactful in communications. He is able to say the proper thing without giving offense and expresses himself in such a way as to decrease apparent threat to others.

indikator.nama: Middle zone width equals middle zone height
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-1a on page 66.
See listing 11-3 on page 66.

The writer talks easily about whatever he feels or thinks. He unburdens himself with words. In many communications this is helpful; however, with his tendency to converse freely, the writer finds it hard to keep secrets.

He speaks freely about anything he knows, and he will elaborate about the more personal aspects of the lives of those he knows as well. He must be expected to reveal confidences to relatives and friends or even acquaintances.

indikator.nama: Ovals clear (no exceptions, all ovals must be clear)
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-2 on page 66.
See listing 05-1 on page 28.

The writer responds impulsively to people and situations and has a tendency to confuse facts. He lacks perspective in viewing circumstances and relationships and ignores possible consequences of his acts. He is restless and tries to crowd too many things into too short a period of time and works by fits and starts with many interruptions. Lack of efficiency, impaired concentration and confusion are the results.

The writer intrudes upon others’ space with little consideration for their rights.

The writer willingly permits others to come close. He likes to be with people, he enjoys working in groups. In fact, he performs best with someone being near or generally with people being around. In his relationships, he is conventional and conforms to the rules of the group. It gives him a sense of security. He adapts himself to circumstances and people, regardless of whether he is in agreement or not.

The writer organizes projects as they are occurring. He works problems out when he is involved with them rather than mentally anticipating them and planning ahead.

The writer’s reactions are based on his feelings in the moment and he is inclined to interpret experiences subjectively. Things are always seen in relation to himself. His own feelings are the ultimate guideline for evaluating everything he senses and sees.
See listing 16-5a on page 99.
See listing 03-2 on page 16.
See listing 17-4a on page 105.
See listing 17-4b on page 105.

Emphasis in handwriting identifies the sphere where the majority of the writer’s interests are centered and from which his ego needs are best filled. Emphasis matches need.

The writer’s interest is more in people than in productivity or intellectual development. Given the choice, he will be with people every time. Working with inanimate objects or information may be a problem. If he is forced through circumstances to work alone most of the day, he needs to balance this by planning recreational social time.

The writer is concerned with the fulfillment of immediate needs rather than planning toward long-range goals. He restricts his interests to what is tangible, realistic and practical from his point of view. Reinforcement of his self-esteem is of foremost concern. He has little motivation to explore outside of this sphere.

Instead of planning ahead, he works with things as they are, adapting, adjusting and improvising as he moves along. He deals with daily life situations and relationships in down-to-earth and practical ways. He is concerned with the realities of the moment and with doing something about what is going on now. Future goals are secondary to the purpose of the moment.

The writer has little interest in improving his level of knowledge. His comprehension may be broad, but it is not high. He is content to stay with what he already knows. He may even resent being asked to think beyond what he is already familiar with. He fails to learn the reasons “why,” or to abstract the knowledge from a situation for future use. He fits best into work where he is fulfilling instant needs and where the immediate is of great concern.
See listing 04-4a on page 22.
See listing 02-6 on page 10.

The writer becomes impulsively involved in projects and relationships, regardless of whether he has the time or the means to sustain such ties. He becomes friendly with too many people and may find himself wasting much time with unimportant relationships.

The writer lives in the present and rarely plans ahead. He responds automatically to stimuli as soon as his interest is aroused.

The writer has an outgoing nature and likes to get involved with people; he enjoys participating in their activities. He expects support from others and finds it difficult to stand alone. He seems like a more kindly individual because of his quick response, and because he seems to be moved by the troubles of others, just as he is by his own.

The writer is emotionally responsive. He has a swift reaction to everything that happens to him and around him. Since he responds so much on the emotional level, he may become prejudiced. He is prone to subjective judgments without examining the facts.

The writer’s responsiveness is valuable in professions such as nursing, reception work, teaching, the healing arts, service organizations, domestic help, and anywhere where he must deal with the public in a service related way.
See listing 03-8a on page 18.
See listing 05-5b on page 30.

He is comfortable with and around others. He is relaxed working alone or in groups. However, he needs a certain amount of solitude before involving himself. He wants to consider the possible consequences of his act.

The writer respects the personal sphere of other people. He anticipates to be treated in the same way. He would resent personal questions that, in his opinion, are too intimate.

The writer thinks in a clear and discerning manner. He is orderly and systematic. He has a feeling for the organization of people and things. He knows how to integrate components into a meaningful whole. He is able to take the parts of an assignment and make them work in consonance with other parts.

(Balanced word spacing is one indicator of above average intelligence.)
See listing 05-1 on page 28.
See listing 16-5 on page 99.

The writer is accommodating with others due to insecurity. He will try to sound out people as to their viewpoints before getting involved or committing himself.

With initial garlands used excessively, the writer is emotionally immature. He submits to other people's views and principles to ensure their liking and support.
See listing 03-3 on page 16.
See listing 02-3 on page 16.

indikator.nama: Letter height decreasing toward end of word
indikator.keterangan: See listing 17-6 on page 101.
See listing 17-4a on page 105.
See listing 17-4b on page 105.

indikator.nama: Lower zone without distortions, or angular, or arcaded forms
indikator.keterangan: (Distorted, angular or arcaded formations would point to anxiety in interpersonal relationships, or the writer would be insecure and self-protective. Lack of these indicators means absence of these characteristics.)

indikator.nama: Lower zone loops return to baseline
indikator.keterangan:
The writer has well developed interpersonal relationships (word spacing, letter spacing, form of loop and primary and secondary pressure need to be evaluated to come to this conclusion.) If the loops are well developed, this indicates sexual interest and fulfillment in the sexual sphere.

The writer is able to use his imagination productively. He learns from past experiences and therefore can apply lessons from the past beneficially to similar situations in the present.
See listing 18-8 on page 110.

indikator.nama: Margin on right narrower than margin on left
indikator.keterangan: The writer gets caught up in relationships and projects. He goes forward to meet people, new situations and life in general with openness, zeal and interest.
See listing 18-9a on page 111.
See listing 03-9 on page 18.
See listing 17-9 on page 106.
See listing 05-5b on page 30.
See listing 18-10b on page 111.
See listing 05-2b on page 28.
See listing 05-2a on page 28.
See listing 05-2d on page 29.
See listing 05-2c on page 28.

The writer has an emotional reaction to anything that stimulates his senses. He enjoys leisure and comfort, he is pleasure loving and sensuous. Likewise, he has an emotional response to suffering, either his own or that of others, and he has lasting emotional memories. What he sees, tastes, smells, hears, or touches, triggers the memory of similar experiences he had before. Sympathy, sorrow, anger, joy and happiness, all last longer with him. The memories of these occurrences then determine how he reacts.

The writer may not be aware of the important role that the emotional memory plays in his daily life. It has become a natural part of him. It affects him so much that he may never be able to learn from a certain situation or person, even though he seldom realizes that he feels for or against circumstances or people, strictly on the basis of emotional memory and that he carries emotionally based grudges and prejudices.

Width of the ductus is an important factor in personal relationships because it affects the whole behavior pattern. Sense impressions are at the heart of a person's comfort or discomfort. It determines culture, the kind of music liked, the kind of clothing chosen, and how the food should be seasoned. It may affect the nature of hobbies. Misunderstandings are almost inevitable and may get blown out of proportion because people with opposing scores simply cannot “tune in” to how the other one feels. They will annoy each other unwilling in so many ways that it is just a question of time until a serious quarrel erupts.

Broad writing without pressure shows that the writer enjoys comfort and leisure and usually is easy-going and relaxed. He is friendly, most of the time, because he wants to get along with others without friction or argument. He avoids exertion wherever possible, conserving his energies for selective use. He seeks an experience strictly for the sensual feeling it gives him. He relishes it and, if possible, wants to repeat it.

Being surrounded by harmony and attractiveness gives the writer a feeling of pleasure and peace. He takes music or some form of art seriously. And because he responds so strongly to what he likes, he suffers equally from feelings he dislikes.

The writer often tries to escape from sensations that upset him. Discord, emotional suffering, or disorder make him want to go to some other place geographically, seeking the harmonious atmosphere he craves.
See listing 16-5a on page 99.

indikator.nama: Final garlanded strokes do not reach above middle zone apex
indikator.keterangan:
With final garlanded strokes reaching above the middle zone apex into the upper zone the writer has an excessive need for attention.

Absence of this indicator means that the writer can devote attention away from himself onto other people.
See listing 03-2 on page 16.
See listing 05-5a on page 30.
See listing 17-4b on page 105.

indikator.nama: Middle zone width equals middle zone height
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-1 on page 67.
See listing 18-9a on page 111.
See listing 03-8a on page 18.

indikator.nama: Score for Interpersonal Involvement (# 18) is 5.0 or higher.
indikator.keterangan: The writer is people oriented. His friends and family mean a lot to him. He is a more sympathetic appearing person, and he is moved by the troubles of others, just as he is by his own. (Other scores have to be taken into consideration. The writer may be superficially warm to protect his self-esteem, or fulfill his ego needs, or he may have high dependency needs).

indikator.nama: Score for Adaptability (# 16) is 5.0 or higher.
indikator.keterangan: The writer has the ability to adapt in situations and with others when and where it is required. He is accommodating and willing to yield to the justified desires of others. He is more open to compromise.

indikator.nama: Signature and ppl without self-protective strokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-9a on page 70.

indikator.nama: Signature and/or ppl without encircling strokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-9b on page 71.
See listing 08-1a on page 52.
See listing 01-1 on page 3.

Hooks in finals are basically left tending. They are so-called back-to-self strokes and reveal self-protective tendencies. They also imply tenacity, clinging to the familiar and self-interest. Most frequently, the writer's tenacity is detrimental for his environment. The writer literally “hooks into” a matter or circumstance for egotistical reasons. He does not want to let go of something from which he hopes to gain a personal advantage.

The writer is tenacious. He hangs onto what he is doing, or trying to do. Once the decision has been made and the job has begun, it is hard to shake him loose.

Tenacity for the writer can be good or bad, depending on the situation, and the principles involved. When he is holding on for the right reasons, this adds to the firmness of his character. On the other hand, if he is inflexible for the wrong reasons, this trait may keep him from being able to shift gears and get back on the right track. He does not know when to let go. He continues when things no longer work to his advantage or when others who are important to him refuse to cooperate.
See listing 01-5 on page 4.

indikator.nama: Letters t and f tied with loop
indikator.keterangan: The writer is persevering in a chosen course and enduring in the face of opposition. He keeps trying against obstacles and rarely accepts defeat. Once committed, he does not easily give up.
See listing 08-3 on page 53.

The writer has endurance. He is interested in the physical aspects of life and in material things. He desires tangible evidence of success. He values what life has to offer and strives to obtain what he can through diligence and effort. Because of his physical orientation, most of his energies are expended in the area of productivity and/or sex.

The writer plans his projects as he goes along rather than organizing mentally in advance. It is difficult for him to stay with mental work for a long period of time. His initial reaction to anything is usually on the bodily level and he will take action to work something out. It irritates him to be inactive. He is built with more stamina and more physical “get up and go.” He can take more exercise without feeling fatigued and he has more recuperative strength. He is usually interested in sports, endurance contests or tests of stamina. His body gives him good support when he places demands on it.

Vocationally, the writer is best suited for fields that are active and vigorous on the physical level such as transportation, communication, sales, law enforcement, engineering, or construction work.
See listing 08-5b on page 53.

indikator.nama: Pressure displaced into lower zone upstrokes
indikator.keterangan:
The writer is sublimating much of his sexual drive into rationally directed activity such as productivity. Such displacement does not occur spontaneously. It is strictly an act of will. Centering all of his energies by will, the writer makes a special effort to excel and takes on increasing vocational responsibilities.

Rather than toward long range goals, the writer applies his efforts toward daily, immediate gains. He uses initiative and aggressiveness to achieve a continuing string of successes. Once a goal has been achieved, he immediately pursues another aim. He keeps forever trying to advance and make “the best of himself.”

The writer assumes that if he really tries, he can achieve everything he is after. He refuses to admit limitations on his part and tries harder than is needed, most of the time. He pushes action rather than letting things unfold and expends a disproportionate amount of strength overcoming obstacles that may not exist. He exerts effort “against the current,” so to speak. There exists a disturbance of inner harmony which the writer tries to re-establish through artificial compensation.

indikator.nama: Pressure in lower zone downstrokes increasing
indikator.keterangan:
The writer is doggedly persistent. His determination steadily increases as he becomes involved in a task. He is like an athlete who husbands his energies and gives his all during the final stretch.

Important! The writer’s determination is not necessarily positive. With negative writing, persistence may be used in an unfavorable, destructive way.
See listing 05-8a on page 31.

indikator.nama: Upper zone downstrokes straight instead of curved ending firmly at the baseline
indikator.keterangan:
The writer is firmly resolved in purpose and action. He is loyal to his beliefs and positive about that which he has chosen. And since his decisions are the result of a deliberate thinking process, they are very important to him. Once his mind is made up and his attitude is fixed, it is hard to sway him from his course.

The writer is faithful to his promises. He is the type who labors steadfastly to make relationships work “in sickness and in health, for better or for worse.” If he is betrayed, he feels devastated and may turn against the people who let him down.

The writer works to advantage in fields such as exploring, missionary work, or developing new breakthroughs in industry and business.

With the indicator very strong, the writer may be an extremist or fanatic. Headstrong and obstinate, he will not listen to reason and has little “give” under pressure. He refuses to compromise, even doing so would be to his advantage.

indikator.nama: Letters f and p with lower part broader than upper
indikator.keterangan:
The writer's orientation is toward his own independent projects. He likes to be involved in several projects at the same time. He organizes his work as he goes along rather than spending time and energy to plan ahead. He is able to develop alternatives in planning or problem solving as problems occur.

With the f-loop toward the right (f), the writer's projects usually pertain to wealth. He worries about money; not money he owes, but money he wants to make in the future.

With a heavy pressured f-loop toward the right (f), the writer has unconscious drives only money can satisfy — the urge for security and that peace of mind that only a substantial savings account can provide.

indikator.nama: Letters f and p with lower part longer than upper
indikator.keterangan: The writer is a realist and doer. He finds most of his ego-satisfying experiences in the area of productivity. He does not get lost in futile speculations; he sees reality as it is. He is very capable of dealing with the pressures of daily life.

The writer's focus is on physical activity. He feels compelled to do, accomplish and produce. Time seems wasted on theory when results count most in life.

Instead of planning ahead, he organizes projects as he goes along. He stays away from mental considerations that slow him down, block him, or could bring him into a negative state of mind. Once a goal has been set, he starts working on it and keeps himself moving toward it until it is achieved. He is at a disadvantage in situations that require more careful planning before action begins.

The writer is naturally active. He enjoys doing physical things. Activity gives him a sense of well-being and aliveness. If he is merely sitting, he feels unproductive and becomes frustrated or begins to brood. Hard work invigorates him; so does running, walking, swimming, hugging, gardening, or any activity that associates his body with the rest of the world. He is built with more stamina and he has more recuperative strength. His body gives him good support when he places demands on it. He can take more physical activity without feeling fatigued. Short breaks for relaxation serve as well as long periods of sleep for other folks. He performs best where he can act rather than think. It is more difficult for him to rise to mental challenges and it is hard for him to stay with mental activity for a long period of time. He learns best through demonstration and by example.

Vocationally, he fits best where he can be active on the physical level. Transportation, sales, law enforcement or construction work would be ideal.

The writer may encounter conflicts in relationships with more mentally oriented people. They tend to feel that he is pressuring them into what he wants without considering their needs.
See listing 21-7 on page 122.
See listing 04-4a on page 22.

indikator.nama: Margin at bottom narrower than upper margin
indikator.keterangan:
With an emphasized (long) lower zone, the writer is productivity oriented. He becomes absorbed in projects and relationships. He is active, motivated, and cherishes material possessions as evidence of success.

With a de-emphasized (short) lower zone, the writer is still productivity oriented, but he suffers from a low level of physical energy. He is apprehensive about unfamiliar projects and afraid of discarding the old and well-known for the new. He prefers the status quo and clings to established routines because of the feelings of security they provide.
See listing 07-3 on page 46.
See listing 08-5b on page 53.

The writer has energy in reserve which can be called on when needed. His determination increases the more he becomes involved in projects. When faced with an obstacle, he has the stamina to make an extra effort to succeed
See listing 07-4 on page 46.

indikator.nama: Pressure displaced into lower zone upstrokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 21-8b on page 123.

indikator.nama: Right tendency in the lower zone
indikator.keterangan: The writer’s instinctual drives are aggressively directed toward the outside world instead of into sexual activities. His energies are channeled into productivity and achievement.

indikator.nama: Score for Functional Ability Syndrome is 4.5 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer feels confident with people and able to face new or difficult circumstances. He is sure of his own talents and potential. He is able to communicate and usually not afraid to speak his mind. He has conscious control, integrity and the ability to perform productively.
See listing 05-5b on page 30.
See listing 13-2a on page 83.
See listing 07-1 on page 46.
See listing 13-2a on page 83.

indikator.nama: Margin on right narrower than margin on left
indikator.keterangan: See listing 19-7b on page 114.

indikator.nama: Margin on right narrowing toward bottom of page
indikator.keterangan: See listing 08-4a on page 53.

The writer has large ego demands and a strong need for recognition. He will work hard for reinforcement of his self-esteem. His rewards come from being noticed and recognized. He is primarily concerned with the present; what is going on right now is of prime importance. He enjoys working with people and before the public, and compliments and praise enhance his performance. If others demonstrate to him that they have noticed he is doing well and that they approve of him, he will try especially hard to do a fine job.

The writer shifts projects and subjects easily to accommodate what he feels is important in the moment. In fact, it is normal for him to do more than one thing or job at the same time. He may be impatient and he has a shorter attention span.

To others, he may appear inconsiderate when he interrupts them or demands them to refocus to meet his immediate needs.

His pattern of learning and working is by fits and starts with many interruptions, both created and allowed.

With middle zone width equal to middle zone height, the writer is very confident and capable. He presumes his own authority and is threatened only by very large responsibilities.

The writer is progressive. He has bigger concepts and thinks in bigger terms. He is particularly competitive in situations where the reward is applause or prestige. He does whatever serves to enhance his ego. For instance, he may be generous in situations where generosity can be used to enhance his self-esteem.

The writer works to advantage in situations that call for leadership. He feels stimulated by large challenges. This does not mean that he does not know fear. In fact, when an immense challenge blocks his way he may, indeed, be very much afraid. And since

he has not felt self-doubt before, it is unfamiliar to him and he does not know how to handle it. He feels temporarily confused and completely frustrated. In other words, when the “large” writer feels fear, it is an unfamiliar experience and he perceives it more intensely than anyone else.

The writer has a healthy personal attitude about who and what he is. He feels assured and comfortable with others and himself. He can communicate, adjust and adapt with a minimum of stress. He is able to interact spontaneously and naturally with superiors and peers. He feels all human beings are worthwhile and valuable, including himself. He has no trouble satisfying his ego needs. He can express them openly and give and receive ego strokes. While he appreciates recognition when it is deserved, he does not constantly beg approval from others to prove his worth. He does not have to impress other people, appease them, or fight them. Without being hostile, the writer avails himself of the space he feels he deserves. He does not allow others to push him around.

The writer expresses his emotions spontaneously and openly. The more intense the inner feelings, the stronger the outward display. It is easy for anyone around him to tell what he is feeling just by looking or listening to him. Whatever the emotion within, positive or negative, it is likely to show without.

The writer is receptive to new ideas and procedures. He is progressive and willing to take risks in order to work something out. He freely shares suggestions and thoughts and he can speak up to defend what is important to him.

With small middle zone height, the writer is still comfortable with others and himself; however, he is most content working by himself, according to his own time schedule. His orientation is toward research, study and things, rather than people. Instead of public acceptance, he seeks goals that offer him gratification and increase his self-esteem.
See listing 07-4 on page 46.

indikator.nama: Pressure displaced into lower zone upstrokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 21-8b on page 123.

The writer’s orientation is toward the future. Independent in his thinking, he is progressive and unconventional. His thoughts and actions are directed toward the future and outward toward the environment. He has extroverted tendencies and he is foremost concerned with the external world of things and people.

indikator.nama: Right tendency in the lower zone
indikator.keterangan: See listing 22-8 on page 128.
The writer is a more secure individual with progressive tendencies. (This needs to be confirmed through other indicators in the writing). Such writers are impatient with detail work.

indikator.nama: Score for Comprehension (# 9) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer has quick comprehension, insight, and the ability to make fast decisions. Able to comprehend new ideas and situations without difficulty, he knows immediately if the information he has been given can be used. He assimilates it with what he knows and puts it to immediate and profitable use.

indikator.nama: Score for Personality Integration (# 13) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer courageously seeks novel experiences. He can tolerate a reasonable degree of risk and uncertainty. If he fails, he is not devastated by the failure. He considers defeat a learning experience which helps him to succeed more readily in the future.

indikator.nama: Signature and/or ppl without self-protective strokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-9a on page 70.

indikator.nama: Signature and/or ppl without encircling strokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 11-10b on page 71.

An elaborated signature or ppl shows that the writer in vain and boastful and extremely conscious of the impression he makes. It reveals self-overestimation and pretense. The absence of these indicators demonstrates that the writer behaves unpretentious and naturally.

The writer is mentally efficient and gets to the heart of a matter at once. Instead of making situations complicated, he simplifies them. He is resourceful in a practical way. He identifies a problem and then looks for the best available solution.

The writer is a productive worker who concentrates on what is necessary and gets it done. His fast pace may not always be obvious because he devises so many shortcuts. He uses progressive means to streamline methods of operation and applies his energies

economically to benefit his work. He works in such a manner that the desired result will be obtained speedily without lessening of competence. With him, there exists always a satisfactory ratio between expended effort and resulting success.

The writer is matter-of-fact in interpersonal relationships. He expresses what he feels directly and without embellishments. Clarity is his chief concern in sharing feelings and ideas and content is more important than style.
See listing 06-2a on page 36.

indikator.nama: Connective forms original from middle to upper zone
indikator.keterangan: See listing 06-2d on page 37.
See listing 16-3 on page 98
See listing 09-2 on page 57.
See listing 06-10c on page 43.
See listing 06-3a on page 37.
See listing 07-1 on page 46.
See listing 10-9a on page 63.

indikator.nama: Lower zone looped and loops return to baseline
indikator.keterangan: See listing 03-7a on page 18.
See listing 04-4a on page 22.
See listing 04-4b on page 10.
See listing 23-6a on page 134.
See listing 23-10 on page 135.
Most of the writer’s ideas are unconventional and original. He is open-minded and his thinking processes move freely and spontaneously. There may be creative ability.
See listing 06-3d on page 38.

The writer proliferates ideas.. As a resource, he is remarkable. He is full of suggestions on any subject which interests him.

(Without supporting traits such as determination, willpower, persistence) But when it comes to driving something into final form, he often lacks momentum. He allows his ideas to back up on him and may be guilty of much unproductive day-dreaming.

The writer thinks in an informal and unorthodox manner but may allow too much room for too many concepts. This makes it difficult for him to think logically and objectively.

The writer adjusts easily to change and is much slower to become irritated or upset. He is easy going about rules and regulations and takes a broader view on matters of right and wrong. His tendency is to put up with too much before disciplining himself and others.

For the writer, imagination may have both good and bad aspects which need to be understood. While he benefits in many ways, he is at a disadvantage when the same imagination amplifies the negative for him. He may increase his own worth imaginatively. He may consider himself more gifted or more important than he is. This self-admiration makes him vulnerable to criticism, either real or implied.

With exaggeratedly broad loops, the writer is mislead by his own imaginings. He scatters his thoughts in too many directions and never seems to have enough time to carry them through in reality.

The broader the loops, the more removed from reality he is. In extreme cases, there may be delusions of grandeur, fantasies, withdrawal and, of course, exaggeration to a great degree.

If the writer allows negative pictures to overwhelm him, he may suffer severe anxiety. Negative imagination may even impair physical functioning.
See listing 08-1a on page 52.
See listing 08-1b on page 52.
See listing 06-10c on page 43.
See listing 06-10d on page 43.
See listing 05-4 on page 29.
See listing 13-2b on page 83.
See listing 05-7 on page 30.

The writer has a good sense of timing and is realistic about his abilities. He plans his activities to ensure the most economic use of his resources and energies. He has a careful outlook in every area of his life. Before becoming involved in a project, he allows himself sufficient time to plan and organize. He considers all ramifications of the undertaking to be certain that a better than average chance for a successful outcome exists.

The writer is discriminating in his dealings with other people. He holds back until he knows just where he stands. He needs time and space until he has checked out the situation and has made a conscious decision to either join or withdraw from a relationship.
See listing 07-3 on page 64.
See listing 08-5b on page 53.
See listing 07-4 on page 46.

indikator.nama: Pressure displaced into upper zone upstrokes
indikator.keterangan: See listing 04-7a on page 23.
See listing 05-8a on page 31.
See listing 07-6b on page 47.
See listing 07-8a on page 48.

indikator.nama: Upper zone height/lower zone length balanced
indikator.keterangan: See listing 13-10 on page 85.
See listing 18-10b on page 111.
See listing 06-10b on page 42.

The writer's feelings are easily bruised. It takes very little to get “under his skin.” He is vulnerable even to unintended slights concerning his personal habits, mannerisms, physical attributes, or manner of dress. It is hard for him to deal with others naturally because he is so affected by what they do and say, and even by the way they say it.

The writer has an unrealistic fear of being criticized in regard to his personal habits, mannerisms, physical attributes, or manner of dress. He exaggerates trivial incidents and fabricates painful episodes in his mind. He believes that others are saying hurtful things on purpose, strictly to provoke or irritate him.

The writer is overly sensitive to any sign of criticism pertaining to his code of ethics, his philosophical beliefs, vocational performance, or his plans and goals.
He is vulnerable to any sign of rejection, a laugh, a shrug, an unfriendly tone of voice. He tries to adjust by withdrawing from situations in which he could get hurt or by building up a wall of defenses around himself.

The writer has an unreasonable dread of being criticized in regard to his code of ethics, his philosophical beliefs, vocational performance, or his plans and goals. His magnified fear leads to various forms of defenses to shield the writer's pride, among them withdrawal, procrastination, and evasiveness.

The writer suffers from lack of mental discipline. He disregards what he considers insignificant. His disregard of details can result in entirely wrong conclusions.
With jabbed i-dots or entangled loops, the writer is very nervous. He cannot focus on any one project for an extended period of time. He finds it hard to listen to someone without jumping in with comments as to what he believes he heard, or what he thought the other person was going to say. He rushes into projects before understanding the nature of a case. Lack of efficiency, impaired concentration and confusion are the result.
See listing 01-10c on page 6.

With fast writing, jabbed periods confirm speed.
With slow writing, the writer is irritable. He wants to shut out what is happening around him to protect himself against the rising tension within. Instead of working productively, he is very likely to fight others who seem to be blocking him. While he can go ahead and work on familiar jobs, he finds it hard to concentrate on new or unfamiliar task. He is not directing himself, he is only reacting. He is prone to make wrong decisions until he is able to relax and become free of the strain that is bothering him.

indikator.nama: Diacriticals pressure heavier than rest of writing
indikator.keterangan: A dot that has extra time spent on it is evidence of a pause in the person's thinking. The writer is preoccupied with something that is irritating to him (extra heavy pressure) or that has aroused his hostility (ground in dot). He is unable to express these feelings of anger and the repressed emotions are creating tension within.

indikator.nama: Final strokes are left tending half ovals
indikator.keterangan:
These strokes occur only in slow writing.
The writer is basically insecure. To protect himself, he is defensively hypocritical and suspicious. He is wary, shrewd and calculating at the same time. He tries to manipulate people to his own advantage and uses little discrimination in the means he employs to serve his own end.

indikator.nama: Initial strokes are long and hooked
indikator.keterangan: The writer habitually resists. He is constantly on the offensive and seeking confrontations. He is constantly waiting for an opportunity to criticize and blame.

The writer is compelled by fleeting impulses and has poor self-discipline. He is swayed by his moods of the moment and unpredictable in his reactions. He finds it difficult to concentrate and to control himself at will. His impulses get the better of him and dominate him completely.

The writer suffers inner conflicts and frustrations. His feelings of self-worth alternate rapidly, either because of influences from the outside or because of mood changes within himself. He goes from feelings of self-assurance to inadequacy within a very short span of time. He deals with his environment according to how secure of insecure he feels in a given moment. He is particularly changeable in situations where he feels vulnerable. The writer vacillates in his degree of involvement. In his confident mood he becomes engrossed in projects but when self-doubts assail him he feels completely inadequate. In that frame of mind, he may reverse his past decisions and as a result gain the reputation for being unreliable. When the switch to the lower plateau happens, he will be noticeably less thorough and much more unsure of his abilities in any situation. (Extreme irregularity may be one criterion for mental illness.)

The writer lacks self-directive ability. He is driven by contradictory impulses and controlled by the mood of the moment. He is unable to discipline himself to wholeheartedly pursue an aim. He finds it difficult to concentrate or control himself at will. His impulses get the better of him and rule him completely. His energies are more or less wasted because he does not know how to use them economically.
With extreme irregularity, the writer's sense of reality may be disturbed, either due to the effect of alcohol, drugs or mental imbalance.
Important! Irregular alignment may be the result of a serious loss through the death of a beloved family member or person. After the grief subsides, line alignment usually returns to normal.

This is left tending since it narrows the oval.
The writer suffers tension in the emotional sphere and anxiety in interpersonal relationships. He feels much hostility resulting in the desire to humiliate others. He is easily offended and sometimes vindictive in personal matters.
Important! If it is the only area of angularity, it does not relate to health problems.

The writer tends to deceive himself instead of others. Because he cannot tolerate the pain that acknowledging reality would produce, he either denies it or assigns a more acceptable reason to unpleasant facts. These spurious excuses are usually plausible but they are not the whole truth. They tend to put circumstances or the writer in a more favorable light.
The fallacy is that the writer tends to build on these distorted images and eventually is unable to relate realistically to his surroundings.
The writer is emotionally insecure. He may be devious and manipulating in order to gain a personal advantage. (This is especially true with long hooked strokes from the baseline or below.)

The encircling stroke is a combination of a protection stroke above and a leftward turning underlining stroke below the baseline. Its significance is far more serious than the meaning of either one of these strokes by themselves. The writer symbolically creates a magical circle around himself and prevents scrutiny not only from left and right but also from above and below.
Often, covert hostility leads to this defense. The writer senses his own ill will and projects it onto others. Such people can be extremely dangerous.
The writer is very much afraid. He does not know where an alleged “attacker” might hide and therefore tries to protect himself on all sides. He overcompensates and turns into an attacker out of fear.

The writer feels uncomfortable with himself and he is dissatisfied with life. His personality is poorly integrated and his behavior maladaptive. Even slight pressure puts him under severe stress. The writer typically has little insight into the reasons for his difficulties.
See listing 26-6c on page 150.

The writer suffers from mental inefficiency and his planning is erratic. He fluctuates between objectivity and subjectivity in evaluating situations and relationships. He can neither maintain desirable contacts nor keep proper distance. He lacks the inner discipline to maintain boundaries that have been established.

The writer is unpredictable in his emotional responses to people. He is inconsistent in considering their emotional needs. He has a fluctuating attitude regarding other people's behavior or working methods. At one time, he may be enthusiastic about their style, while at another time he may insist upon his own routine.

The writer fluctuates between being overly dependent upon others and being contact-shy. He is changeable in the pursuit of practical aims and in his thinking processes. Sometimes he smoothly links thoughts while at other times he is unable to associate ideas.

The writer has a strong need for security. One of the results is a fluctuating attitude towards productivity and sex. He may be excited about a project and then suddenly, for no obvious reasons, become discouraged. His motivation to complete projects depends upon the task, his degree of familiarity with it and how well he knows the outcome of it. He is more inclined to persist in familiar activities than in undertakings that are new and therefore risky. He may stay with a project for fear of losing face. Sometimes he needs help when a job turns out to be too tough. At other times, he needs encouragement when a projects lasts too long and his interest threatens to fade. He especially needs reassurance when his ego seems threatened if he continues and fails. In stressful situations, the writer would rather find excuses to give up, procrastinate, or give the job to somebody else rather than continue and “make a fool of himself.” If he does continue, he expects and needs a great deal of approval, attention, praise and support. The writer suffers much frustration (because of giving up on projects) and/or tension (because of continuing under stress).
See listing 26-6b on page 149.
The writer's sense of self-worth is fluctuating widely, particularly in interpersonal relationships. He goes from feelings of self-assurance to inadequacy within a very short span of time.

The writer fluctuates between feelings of inner assurance and inadequacy. At times, he is courageous and certain. He feels comfortable with people and is able to interact spontaneously and naturally. He can communicate with a minimum of stress. At other times, in similar situations and/or with the same people, he feels ill at ease. He is inhibited and restrained. He is aware of his alleged limitations and worries about them. He is afraid to volunteer ideas even if he thinks they are worthwhile. When in that frame of mind, he seeks familiar things and familiar people for security.

The writer's emotions are too erratic to be checked by self-discipline. In the area of interpersonal relationships, he fluctuates between feelings of assurance and inferiority. The result is that he is unpredictable in his reactions. He may respond spontaneously and be outgoing at one time and inhibited and withdrawn in a similar situation.

The writer's level of available energy fluctuates. He applies it in an inconsistent and uneconomical manner. He seems to have sudden bursts of strength which seem to die down as quickly as they flare up. The degree of willpower he brings to a task is inconsistent. At times he applies an inordinate amount of force while at other times his resolution falters. He may have little endurance for completing tasks.

The writer suffers tension much of the time. Frustration and personality conflicts interfere with healthy personality integration. They hinder effective functioning and constructive accomplishment.

With extremely irregular pressure, the writer has deeply ingrained neurotic tendencies. He is tense, inflexible and impulsive. He lacks control and has little endurance. Frustrated much of the time, his inner conflicts interfere with healthy personality integration.

The writer vacillates in his productive output. He makes his greatest effort when he feels himself observed. Consciously or unconsciously, he tries to call attention to his remarkable effort. As soon as he is no longer being watched he relapses into a less strenuous pace.

The writer has unexpected emotional responses. He is confused about his own reaction to outside stimuli and his changing moods. He suffers from a constant state of inner irritation and finds it hard to concentrate. Much of his energy is being exhausted by this inner conflict.
See listing 26-6a on page 1.

The writer vacillates in his attitudes and inner motivations. At one time, he thinks independently, while in a similar situation he may cling to traditional values. One day he is stimulated by intellectual pursuits while at another time he becomes mentally bored. At times he is motivated to achieve and eager to advance himself. Then his mood changes and he no longer thinks in terms of getting ahead.

The writer suffers conflict in interpersonal relationships. He varies in how much contact he allows himself to establish with his environment. Sometimes he lets people get close and sometimes he shuts them out. His mood swings can range from a pathological need for solitude to a constant need for being surrounded by people.

When the counter stroke causes a letter to take on the character of another letter, or when it results in a peculiar structure, the interpretation is negative. The less obvious the reversal, for instance in the middle of a word, the more negative is the meaning.
The writer tends to mislead others. He uses alibis and excuses. He turns facts around and will deny obvious truths.

indikator.nama: Counter strokes open toward the left
indikator.keterangan: The writer is egocentric. In his dealings in others he acts in such a way that he will always “leave himself a way out.”

indikator.nama: Final strokes extending underneath the following word
indikator.keterangan: The writer engages in "psychological speculation". He is trying to manipulate others by guessing their motivations.

indikator.nama: Final strokes are left tending half ovals
indikator.keterangan: See listing 26-5a on page 149.
The writer vacillates between friendliness and egotistical behavior. If necessary, he will fake civility while in reality, he is harsh and rancorous and often, he makes a covert effort to resist.
See listing 03-3 on page 16.
The writer tends to hide, conceal and cover up. He uses calculated friendliness to further his own interests.

The writer's behavior is characterized by duplicity and pretense. He hides deceptive intentions behind a facade of sham sincerity.

(When only a few supported angles creep in, almost without the person being aware of it, the implication is especially grave. In such a case, artfulness has become an inherent part of the writer's nature; he is cunning and manipulative.)

Rolled strokes are one of the indicators of insincerity. They are related to deception and hypocrisy.
The writer is overly concerned with the impression he makes on other people. He will pose and pretend in order to manipulate the opinion others hold of him.
See listing 03-4 on page 17.
The writer manipulates others by intentionally disguising his true intentions. (This indicator is especially serious in combination with threadlike formations.)

The relative success of the “spoon e” writer may be based upon left-over infantile drives. Unfulfilled love needs as well as oral desires may trigger the yearning for money and possessions. The writer's fear of being unable to handle life's exigencies effectively may turn him into a smooth and calculating manipulator.

The writer is covetous, artful and evasive while outwardly, he manages to appear proper and correct. Most often, he senses the reaction of others and adopts the appropriate behavior to gain his own advantage. And he adapts without complaint because foremost, he wants to remain inconspicuous.

Important! Many of the “spoon-e” writers are basically capable people. Like animals, they use all available means instinctively to take care of their own needs. They pursue their goals covertly and persistently. Any trace of intrigue is cleverly concealed. Usually gains are small, but frequent. Calculated friendliness is the bait covering the hook. It is a smokescreen to hide the writer's true motivation.
(Few burglars use “spoon e's.” As a rule, “spoon-e” writers are more intelligent and if they turn to criminal activities, are more likely to be embezzlers.)

indikator.nama: Score for Empathy (#20) is 5.0 or higher and score for Interpersonal Involvement (#18) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is not a people person. He manipulates people for his own ends. He is an observer, disengaged, and his empathy is negative. He uses what he can sense about people for his own ends.

The writer is defensive and tries to conceal certain matters of personal concern. He communicates only in the most indirect manner. Under stress, he is likely to manipulate, blame others, lie or resort to silence to evade the truth. The writer's evasiveness is often infantile in character. It represents a defense he has carried over from childhood into his adult life.

The writer is defensive. He uses excuses or alibis. He manipulates, blames other people or lies. He tries to mislead others and wants to obscure his real intents from those with whom he deals. Frequently, deceitfulness has become a habitual pattern of disguise.

Important! With distorted loops in the lower zone there may be frequent preoccupation with sexual matters.
See listing 26-8b on page 146.
See listing 02-10b on page 12.

The writer is basically very anxious and uneasy. He is intensely concerned about the effect he has on others. His basic attitude is one of fear that someone will see through him and uncover the inner conflicts he refuses to admit to himself. As a result, he constantly tries to manipulate the impression he makes on the outside. He makes a continuing effort to appear so perfect that no one can fault him for anything. To hide vaguely sensed feelings of uncertainty, he makes a frantic attempt to feign composure and keep up an appearance of confidence. The result is a great deal of unnaturalness and his behavior is not spontaneous in any way.

indikator.nama: Loops corrected in the lower zone
indikator.keterangan: The writer wants to cover up problems in the sexual sphere and in the area of productivity. He does not want to admit these deficiencies to himself and he wants to hide them from others at all costs.

indikator.nama: Loops corrected in the upper zone
indikator.keterangan: The writer tries to camouflage his insecurities through over-compensation. He tries to manipulate others’ opinion of him by flaunting his alleged ethical principles and wants to project loftier ideals than he actually has.

The writer suffers from lack of mental discipline. He selects only information he momentarily needs, or depends upon others to gather information for him.. He skims along the surface and is content with superficial knowledge. Ignoring important details can result in wrong conclusions. He rushes in for the results before understanding the nature of a case.

The writer is an opportunist who fails to adopt a definite opinion and shifts sides according to circumstances. He will not let himself be pinned down to a specific standpoint and he is able to talk himself out of almost anything.

When secondary thread turns toward the lower zone it points to instinctual “lawlessness.”

Important! The writer may be working beyond his optimum capacity. He skims along the surface selecting only the most obvious facts. Most of the time, he is content with superficial knowledge. Overlooking important parts can be perilous because it causes him to reach inaccurate conclusions. He suffers from lack of forethought and rushes in for the result before understanding the nature of a case.

The writer is impulsive and acts rashly without looking at possible consequences. He suffers from lack of mental control and has unrealistic feelings of buoyancy. He has a superficial outlook and considers only what is easily apparent and observable.

Important! In slow writing, rising lines may be due to the paper having been placed diagonally in front of the writer. In that case, they have no graphological meaning.
Rising lines may also be due to a vision problem. This possibility should be eliminated before making a diagnosis.
See listing 26-6c on page 153.

The writer habitually exaggerates. It is a natural tendency for him. He is trying to squeeze every ounce of drama out of a situation. The effect he is creating carries him away.
