(The craving for possessions is a defense against anxiety. The need for affection is repressed to such a degree that it no longer appears on the surface. The fear of rebuff is so great that it prevents the writer from letting others know that he would like to have some attention. He has such an overwhelming sense of inadequacy that he will not even admit to himself the need for it. The craving for material things then momentarily or permanently takes its place. To compensate for his lack of self-worth, the writer clings to material things.)

The writer is a sworn enemy of waste and may be unnecessarily mean with money. Foremost concerned with gratifying mundane needs – food, clothing, shelter – he makes himself miserable by the fear of poverty. He may be stingy in dispensing funds to others, even when they are nearest and dearest to him.

He has lost the art of spontaneously giving. While he never seems to lack funds to “fall back on” he never seems to be able to part with money now. He is eager to keep and to hoard. In his miserly concern for tomorrow, he may fail to allow himself the means to enjoy today.

The writer wants to own for the sake of possessing and for the security his belongings represent to him. He wants to hold more than he needs or deserves.

The writer is extremely covetous and tends to collect all kinds of things. He accumulates items he may never have use for but simply cannot throw away. When his possessions are taken from him, he can feel intense anger. The writer hates throwing away anything. (He may overeat to prevent the waste of food. He may buy bargain materials that are of inferior quality simply because he makes a temporary saving by doing so. He combines errands to save expenditures of time and gasoline. Organization may be a problem. There never seems enough room for all the things he accumulates.)

The writer probably has his own system of order and hates having his possessions tampered with. He expects others to refrain handling his belongings or rearranging them without discussing it first.

The writer may be a good provider. As a manager, he will keep things in good repair. Usually, he will be unwilling to loan anything and other people's carelessness with possessions is very distressing to him. Building security is his strong suit. He is miserly and wants to hold onto his funds. He parts with what is his only to trade for the better.

The writer is likely determined to protect himself. He plans ahead and his strategy evolves around security. His foremost concern is about tomorrow's needs. With one eye always on the future, he can become a miser who hoards for tomorrow and fails to live today.

To the writer, success becomes directly associated with material gains and he drives a hard bargain, as a rule. Nothing is too trivial if the bottom line means profit for him. He instinctively seems to feel what will be advantageous to him. His failure to share can cause relationships to become difficult.

Important! Stingy individuals rarely becomes alcoholics. It just does not make sense to them to pour all their resources down the drain.

indikator.nama: Final strokes very brief or non-existent
Final stroke in M's and N's or m's and n's higher than previous strokes
indikator.keterangan:
The writer is very shy and fearful. Afraid to venture beyond narrow limits, he avoids drawing attention to himself.

Pitifully self-conscious, he cannot mix socially without strain. Meeting strangers is nearly impossible for him. Self-effacing and retiring, he usually keeps in the background. Others will hardly notice him in a group.

The writer seldom acts “like he means it.” Due to inner insecurities, he does not have the courage to assert himself. He rarely follows through if other people disagree with him and constantly tries to placate more forceful people in his environment. He has a disconcerting habit of almost apologizing to others for his very existence.

Easily embarrassed or upset, he fails to communicate spontaneously. It is hard for him to share his feelings with others, or let others know that he wants them to respond to him. His statements usually sound like questions.

In situations requiring command, the writer would be ineffective and ill at ease. For that reason, he fits better in jobs where he is little noticed or in positions where no one needs to be subservient to him.

The writer shows a general lack of courage in most of life’s situations. Since he is so anxious under emotional pressure, he feels that he is unable to handle it.

Timidity prevents him from making social contacts and may lead to misconceptions about his personality. Some of his friends may think he is being standoffish, when in reality, he feels uncomfortable in social intercourse.

indikator.nama: Tightly retraced strokes on m's and n's

indikator.keterangan: The writer adheres rigidly to what is traditional and established. His tendency is take absolutely no risks. Afraid of the unknown element in change, he clings to established methods and principles. His views may be orthodox and outdated and may have little application to today's conditions but he sees no reason for changing them. He likes to fall back on the things he can trust.

The letter and word is not crossed out; the individual writes into the letter instead so that a less legible word or structure is created.

The writer is restless and suffers from wandering thoughts. They are due to anxiety and repressed guilt feelings.

He has a tendency toward covering up of character deficiencies which are painful for him to admit. He tries to create a more favorable impression of himself but instead of improving his inner security, he only escalates his difficulties.
See listing 01-10c on page 6.

indikator.nama: Letters or parts of letters or words missing
indikator.keterangan:
The writer suffers from nervous irritability and from the inability to concentrate. He suffers from anxiety with resulting disorganization and diminished thinking ability.

The writer is skillful in hiding the truth. He subjectively interprets facts and leaves out “unpleasant” details.

The writer lacks objectivity and perspective in situations and interpersonal relationships. He reacts impulsively to people and intrudes upon others' space without considering the consequences of his acts.

When a long lower extension overlaps an upper, the writer is involved in too many relationships or interests, or in one or two areas that are complex.

When entanglement results from long upper loops, it indicates superficial interest in intellectual pursuits. There may be escape into a fantasy world, day dreaming, etc. The writer tends to confuse facts and chaotic thinking is one of the results.

Such writers are egotistical, adhere to their own standards and feel a general lack of obligation toward other people and the world in general.

With narrow letter spacing, communication is always diminished. One of the underlying causes may be the writer's unconscious desire to thwart communication. He may not want to open himself to others because of the insecurity that doing so arouses. Another reason may be plain disregard for the others (including the reader). The writer simply does not care whether or not he is understood.

The writer's physical nature governs his personality. He is restless and his tendency is to do something physical all of the time. He finds it difficult to relax; he feels something is wrong when he is not doing something physically. He becomes irritated by inactivity. If working in a sedentary job, he has to shift his position frequently. He may walk about, even while holding a serious conversation. His movements serve to relax the physical body. They have nothing to do with mental inattention, in such circumstances. He may have the habit of yawning or falling asleep while other people are talking or socializing. They may be offended by this alleged slight, especially, when the writer snaps back as soon as something of interest enters the conversation.

The writer hates routine in anything, including sex. He fails to plan ahead and often takes on more than he can accomplish in a given period of time. It would be difficult for him to stay retired from active life or from something that interests him. He functions best in fields that are active and vigorous on the physical level. Transportation, construction work, etc. are desirable jobs.

The writer's orientation is strictly physical. He has a bodily response to every stimulating sensation. Under pressure, he is more inclined to respond with physical activity than to think.

The writer is very restless and needs to be on the go all the time. It bothers him to be inactive. When he does not have a chance to use up his excess energy, he becomes very restless. He cannot relax and moves about without purpose. There may be pointless fidgeting, wriggling and foot or finger tapping. He feels confined when he cannot be up and moving around. He wastes time and irritates others with his aimless wandering.

The writer lives an unscheduled life. He has extremely poor organizational ability. He has too many irons in the fire. His attention shifts from one thing to another and he gets involved in too many projects at the same time. In most cases, confusion is related to tangible, material things and reasons.

The writer hates routine in anything, including sex. Whatever can be predicted, is anathema to him. He may want a lot of sex, want it often, or want it repeatedly (particularly, if loops don't return to the baseline, indicating that he does not get satisfied.) In many instances, it is the desire for a variety of sensations and experiences rather than deep feelings that drives him to sexual contacts.

The writer may place notable importance on origin and heritage.
Important! With the other two zones small, there may be glandular problems.

indikator.nama: Lower zone loops entangle with middle zone of following line
indikator.keterangan: The writer plans poorly and tries to crowd too many things into one day. He works by fits and starts with many interruptions. Lack of efficiency and impaired concentration are the result. He wastes his energies and sets himself up for frustration.
See listing 02-6 on page 10.

The writer tends to exaggerate what he experiences. He over-reacts, distorts and is unrealistic in his views and in the interpretation of what others have said and done. He repeats things in exaggerated form.

The writer is egocentric and views the world strictly from his subjective point of view. He is very sensitive to criticism, both real and imagined. This, in turn, affects his performance, his sex life and his general attitude.

The writer is very restless and becomes entangled in a variety of activities and relationships. He is a poor organizer and gets easily sidetracked and confused. He jumps from one experience to another without fully realizing any of them. He may throw over years of accomplishment just for a thrill.

He gets involved with many different people from many contrasting walks of life. In his sex life, too, he seeks excitement and diversity. It is the variety of sensations rather than deep feelings that drive him to seek many contacts. If a partner is not stimulating, he is quickly turned off and will leave in search for a more provocative mate. He will try anything once and appreciates a partner who is lenient about his “wanderlust.”

With exaggeratedly broad loops, the writer has a highly developed sexual imagination and indulges in sexual fantasies. He may have a vast number of bizarre ideas. Distortion and lack of reality orientation affect all other traits. They also prevent logical thinking.

The writer jumps from one experience to another. He distorts what he remembers without realizing it. He seeks variety on any level. The writer's fleeting interest in too many people and too many things prevents prolonged involvement with anyone or any serious endeavor. Stamina is also decreased.

The writer is usually boastful and theatrical in manner. He needs to attract attention and admiration. He is often sexually disappointing but will talk about his imaginary successes.
See listing 18-8 on page 110.

The writer is unsettled and has poor organizational ability. He lacks a sense of time and the skill for well-ordered procedure. His own schedule is haphazard and he is inconsiderate of other people's plans. He intrudes on their time without specific purpose. He may talk at great length without ever coming to the point. Important! The implication is more serious when so much is written into the margin that a new page would have been indicated. With small writing, the indicator is more significant.
See listing 26-6b on page 149.
See listing 27-8a on page 156.

The writer wants to escape from himself. He is too restless and uneasy to be alone. He leans for support on others and wants to “drown” himself in his surroundings. He does not take the time for emotionally satisfying relationships. He is too driven and rushes headlong into projects or encounters without allowing himself to establish deeper bonds.

With light pressure, the writer is overly curious and inquisitive. His interest in the concerns of others is exaggerated. He busies himself with the affairs of other people to avoid having to think about himself.
See listing 28-10 on page 162.

The writer feels inadequate and is very inhibited. He sets his aspirations in a very limited way. He dreads change and clings to what he already knows. He is fearful to aspire higher than where he presently is. Above all, he seeks to maintain the status quo.

With primary pressure heavy, (particularly with LZ emphasis), details are the writer's main concern. He worries when even petty details are overlooked. He finds is difficult to complete anything to his satisfaction because some minor detail always remains yet to be taken care of.

In most cases, there exists a conflict between the writer's innate ability and his limited aspirations. The result is extreme tension.

The writer feels inadequate and inhibited. He sets his goals in a security minded way. He settles for what seems easily attainable and his goals are based on what kinds of successes he has already had in the past. He focuses mentally on short-range project and is afraid to reach up and take a chance with what seems more difficult to accomplish. He is content with where he is as long as it offers a minimum of security. When he strives for what others disapprove of, either accidentally or impulsively, he experiences guilt and anxiety.
See listing 32-4a on page 187.
See listing 32-10a on page 190.

Horizontal expansion expresses the amount of “elbow room” the writer requires. It demonstrates how much freedom he needs in the physical, mental and emotional sphere in order to function effectively in his day-to-day activities. It reveals how willing he is to share his feelings, time, energy and resources. In a positive context, it indicates confidence, drive, zeal and courage. Negatively, it demonstrates inhibition, calculation, distrust, insincerity and, possibly, deceit.

The writer demands only a small amount of space in which to operate and is comfortable working in a restricted area. He feels uneasy in large gatherings. He limits his field of social activity to people he feels comfortable with. He works best under supervision and is thankful to those who teach him what he needs to know. Because he feels so inhibited himself, he admires courage and strength in others.

With narrow letter width, the writer is hesitant to share with others his time, emotions and energy.

With narrow letter width and broad letter spacing, the writer feels more inhibited in intimate relationships than in social situations.

Horizontal expansion expresses the amount of “elbow room” the writer requires. It demonstrates how much freedom he needs in the physical, mental and emotional sphere in order to function effectively in his day-to-day activities. It reveals how willing he is to share his feelings, time, energy and resources. In a positive context, it indicates confidence, drive, zeal and courage. Negatively, it demonstrates inhibition, calculation, distrust, insincerity and, possibly, deceit.

The writer demands an extremely small amount of space in which to operate. He is easily overwhelmed. Because of the tension he suffers, he severely restricts his field of activity. He takes life in very small doses, especially when it comes to decisions and responsibility. He works best under supervision. He is afraid when faced with much accountability. He prefers to rely on others for the guidance he needs.

With narrow letter width, the writer is miserly in giving. He is unable to share with others, either his resources or himself
See listing 30-7b on page 172.

The writer is very apprehensive. His inner fears make it nearly impossible for him to respond emotionally to other people or to express feelings himself. He feels so vulnerable that he tries to keep his feelings strictly to himself. He does not, under any circumstances, allow others to know of his hurts and fears. He tries to repress emotional display in others, too. He is uptight and rigid, all because he is so afraid

indikator.nama: Lower zone loops do not return to baseline
indikator.keterangan: The writer cannot use his imagination productively. He fails to learn from past experiences and therefore cannot apply lessons from the past beneficially to similar situations in the present. He is inhibited in intimate situations and as a result, may suffer from an incomplete sex life. Despite their very real existence, sexual drives may be either negated or unsatisfactorily expressed.
See listing 32-5 on page 188.
See listing 32-6a on page 186.
See listing 32-7 on page 187.
See listing 31-7 on page 179.

Extremely small middle zone height is the manifestation of severe self-restriction and reveals an extremely poor self concept. In most cases, this discloses either mental or emotional problems, or both.

The writer has an irrational fear of reality. He is inhibited, fearful and humble. He overestimates the magnitude of every-day occurrences and feels powerless to deal with the realities of life.

The writer is vulnerable to criticism that is directed toward him or toward his work. He seeks approval and will strive hard deserve it. Being appreciated makes him feel secure. Much anxiety results from the strain of trying to earn others' respect by surpassing their requirements.

The writer's power of concentration is well developed. Defensively, such concentration may be used as an escape from the discomfort of interpersonal relationships.

With emphasized initials or capitals, the writer is intellectually vain.

At some time in his life the writer has found it necessary to withhold the expression of his emotions. This has become a habit, and now he functions restrained in all emotional circumstances. He is very inhibited and suffers from constant anxiety. Toward the outside world, he is over-controlled and reserved. He is afraid to express his true feelings because he worries about the consequences. He uses defensive behaviors such as evasiveness, suppression and secretiveness. To protect himself, he evaluates each situation in regard to his own security. The writer is especially insecure in interpersonal relationships.

He is self-conscious and timid. He is aware of his alleged limitations and worries about them all the time. Because of the tension he suffers, he tries to restrict his field of social activity. Relationships are limited to people he knows or to individuals where he feels superior and thus more personally at ease. It takes a long time before he feels relaxed in a group, even with people he knows. In public appearances he feels strained and uncomfortable. He remains in a more confined area and is careful not to infringe on others' personal space. Even if he is interested in certain people, it is not easy for him to speak to them.

The writer is ultra-conservative. Change of any kind is threatening to him. He is afraid to volunteer ideas, even when he knows they are worthwhile. He relies on others to give him the information he needs. His conversation is composed mostly of agreements and silence. He seems more eager to hear what other people are saying than to speak himself.

The writer may behave inappropriately under stress. As a result, he often suffers from guilt feelings and remorse. He is egocentric and handles everyday matters in a self-conscious, petty and suspicious manner. His defensiveness holds him back from many possible advances and seriously impedes interpersonal relations and personal growth.
See listing 30-7a on page 171.

indikator.nama: Cover strokes in the middle zone
indikator.keterangan: The writer suffers severe emotional inhibitions in his day-to-day relationships. To protect himself, he limits his field of social activity. He tends to withdraw from situations that make him tense. He has great difficulty satisfying his emotional needs. He can neither give nor receive ego strokes and as a result, may feel guilty and despondent. To keep the guilt feelings repressed he resorts to self-deception and even deceit.
See listing 32-1b on page 186.
See listing 31-9a on page 180.
See listing 31-9b on page 180.

The writer places first priority on his private life. Publicly, he tries to downplay the importance of himself. He wants to appear less significant than he really is. With very broad letter width, he expects that others revere him for the understatement of himself.

indikator.nama: Initials in signature height very low
indikator.keterangan:
The writer places more importance on his private than on his public life. Publicly, he projects an unrealistically humble image of himself. He appears modest and shy and wants to conceal his true capabilities from those with whom he deals.

The writer may feel very insecure in public life, although he may possess very real capabilities.
See listing 31-9e on page 181.

The writer has a strong urge to repress memories of his childhood. Others may have labeled him a slow, clumsy, ugly or stupid youngster. As a result, he has grown up feeling inhibited and inadequate. On the emotional level, he wants to deny these early experiences and get away from the past.

The writer lacks self-esteem. He may be self-conscious and probably prefers to work “behind the scenes” or in support of a stronger person.

indikator.nama: Final stroke in M’s and N’s or m’s and n’s higher than previous strokes
indikator.keterangan: The writer suffers from feelings of inferiority. He rates public figures, society, even strangers, higher than himself. He feels self-conscious and inhibited with unfamiliar people or during social events. His feelings of self-esteem rise or fall quickly according to what he considers others’ opinion of himself.

indikator.nama: Middle zone portion of upper zone letters very short
indikator.keterangan:
The writer emphasizes intellectual activities (this does not verify excellence, just orientation). He feels inhibited with people and tries to escape stress by keeping himself mentally occupied. As a rule, this is a socially acceptable method to avoid spending more time in interpersonal relationships.

With a very large upper zone, this is an attempt to overcompensate for inferiority feelings.

indikator.nama: Copybook style with isolated incongruous forms
indikator.keterangan: The writer is basically conforming and conventional; however, he will have isolated characteristics that cannot be reconciled with his customary behavior. To outsiders, they will seem totally out of character.

indikator.nama: Letter forms dissimilar in similar locations
indikator.keterangan: The writer suffers from poor personality integration. He has contradictory feelings about himself. He is inconsistent in what he feels about a certain situation or how he behaves under given circumstances. He is unable to maintain consistent behavior.

Placement of individual lines to the left or right reveals how often and how long the writer fluctuates between spontaneity and fear.

The writer suffers from conflict regarding his need for security. He fluctuates between inhibition on the one side and spontaneous involvement on the other.
See listing 26-6b on page 149.
See listing 27-4 on page 154.
See listing 27-9 on page 156.
See listing 27-8a on page 156.
See listing 27-6a on page 155.
See listing 27-6b on page 155.
See listing 27-10 on page 156.
See listing 27-3a on page 154.

indikator.nama:
Score for Empathy (#20) is 5.0 or higher and
score for Interpersonal Involvement (#18) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is not a people person. He is more likely to be an observer. His empathy is negative. He may manipulate people and use what he “senses” for his own ends.

indikator.nama:
Score for Empathy (#20) is 5.0 or higher and
score for Friendliness (#19) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer feels for people but the inner conflict restricts him from showing it.

indikator.nama:
Score for Aspirations (# 04) is 5.0 or higher
and score for Inhibitions (# 37) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: Conflicting scores limit the writer's aspirations. The conflict sets up a state of tension when the writer desires to progress. Because of his inhibitions, he is hesitant to move ahead. His usual reaction is to take one step forward and one step back, thus remaining in one spot. If he does get involved, he works under constant strain with the inevitable consequence of becoming unduly fatigued.

indikator.nama:
Score for Ego Needs (#02) is within one point
of score for Inhibitions (# 37)
indikator.keterangan: In combination, these scores limit extroverted tendencies. The writer is extremely tense when becoming involved in either projects or relationships. He wants to but cannot go ahead. While the ego needs to be fed, his inhibitions will not allow it.

indikator.nama:
Score for Self-esteem (#12) is 5.0 or higher and
score for Inhibitions (# 37) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan:
The writer wants to accomplish great things, but his inhibitions will not allow it. His high self-esteem (vanity) may create a false picture of accomplishment in his mind.

With self-confidence above 5.0, he will be relaxed with familiar people. He may also mingle with crowds and unfamiliar people, but inwardly he will feel tense.

indikator.nama:
Score for Interpersonal Involvement (# 18) is 5.0 or higher
and score for Withdrawal (# 32) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer wants to establish contact but also fears rejection. Consequently, he has the tendency to withdraw in situations where he anticipates or imagines rebuff.

indikator.nama: Score for Mental Orientation (# 07) is 2.0 or more points higher than score for Physical Energy (# 22)
indikator.keterangan: The writer is in danger of driving himself beyond his physical limits. The problem is that mental energy cannot be replenished as quickly as it is drained. Mentally driving himself without sufficient physical energy to back up this drive is exhausting on the system. (It could be compared to driving a car on the battery rather than the generator. It works fine until the machine breaks down.)

indikator.nama:
Score for Self-control (# 15) is 5.0 or higher
and score for Vulnerability to Stress Syndrome (# VI) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer does not need such strong rational controls. He is able to handle stress. In this case, the extra control is an added burden which uses up productive energy.

indikator.nama:
Score for Self-control (# 15) is 5.0 or higher
and score for Self-confidence (# 11) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is very demanding of himself. He tries to control personality characteristics that would be detrimental to a favorable self-image. With his high demand for self-mastery, he is very aware of alleged defects or deficiencies in himself which, in turn, increases the poor image he has of himself. This creates tension. Because of his controls, this tension is held within. Only in rare instances will great tension cause an eruption of emotions.

indikator.nama:
Score for Self-control (# 15) is 5.0 or higher
and score for Self-esteem (# 12) is 4.0 or lower
indikator.keterangan: The writer is very demanding of himself. He tries to control personality characteristics that would be detrimental to a favorable self-image. With his high demand for self-mastery, he is very aware of alleged defects or deficiencies in himself which, in turn, increases the poor image he has of himself. He feels unimportant, inadequate, afraid of criticism or derogation by others. This conflict creates tension. Because of the writer's strict controls, this tension is held within. Only in rare instances will great tension cause an eruption of emotions.

The writer feels anxious and slightly threatened all of the time. He is very controlled and unspontaneous to avoid acting “improperly.” Every behavior is carefully thought out. He considers the consequences of his conduct and reflects upon possible repercussions. He holds back until he knows the way is safe.

The writer is extremely careful in his dealings with other people, peers, family, friends, or supervisors. Decision making is difficult because he fears to commit himself. He vacillates and delays until he knows “just where he stands.” He relies on established working methods and follows the same habits in interpersonal relationships. He makes a routine of everything (including sex). If his system is disregarded by others, he is devastated.
See listing 36-1a on page 216.

indikator.nama: Cover strokes in the upper zone
indikator.keterangan: The writer is anxious most of the time. He is self-critical and has feelings of guilt and self-blame. Change is threatening to him because of the risk it involves. He finds security in established beliefs and will not easily change them for new ideas. He is prejudiced and has a strictly “black or white” view of things; he tends to become indignant when others refuse to accept his point of view. His intolerance limits his chance of establishing good relationships and lessens problem solving ability.

indikator.nama: Directional pressure from right in the middle zone
indikator.keterangan: See listing 31-1a on page 177.

indikator.nama: Directional pressure in the lower zone
indikator.keterangan: See listing 31-1b on page 177.

Gaps occur erratically. They are empty spaces that are too broad for the writer’s normal spacing arrangement. The basis for gaps anywhere is anxiety.

The writer is prone to infrequent lapses in concentration due to worry, inhibition and/or anxiety. He over-reacts to distractions from the outside. He has to stop temporarily to recall what he was thinking about before he can continue. 

Important! Gaps cannot be removed through grapho therapy. To eliminate them in a writing, it is necessary to determine what causes the anxiety in the writer’s life and remove the cause.
See listing 32-10c on page 191.

Transposed letters occur with dyslexia. This should be ruled out before attempting a graphological diagnosis.

The writer is experiencing anxiety which interferes with concentration and effective thinking. He is distracted and prone to making unintentional mistakes.

indikator.nama: Last part of one letter is first part of following letter
indikator.keterangan:
The writer suffers from an overwhelming feeling of dread without specific cause for fear. He essentially goes through life frightened. He feels lonely and defenseless in a hostile world. He is afraid of the risks and uncertainties of everyday life. He feels distressed, distracted and sometimes confused. He has trouble sleeping and relaxing.

The writer uses many defensive strategies. The fallacy is that in the long run these create more anxiety than they alleviate.

The writer’s conflicts interfere with his relationships with others. He is so preoccupied with his problems that he cannot concentrate on the concerns of others.

indikator.nama: Downstrokes in letters “m” and “n” are too few or too many
indikator.keterangan: The writer is constantly uptight and anxious. He has feelings of insecurity which he tries to suppress. The constant effort interferes with effective thinking and the ability to concentrate.

indikator.nama: Letters or parts of letters or words missing
indikator.keterangan: See listing 36-2b on page 216.

The writer suffers from anxiety which is almost a preoccupation. He feels worried about the present situation, about hazards to his security, and about his handling of interpersonal relationships. The continuity of his thinking is disturbed. He suffers from mental exhaustion and experiences memory lapses. His ability to concentrate is poor.

If the writing is segmented through the omission of upstrokes, the writer is trying to burn all bridges between himself and the world at large. If the lower zone is segmented, the writer tries to avoid close contacts on the physical level.

These loops are usually seen in the handwritings of people who find their partner sexually unsuitable or unsatisfactory. When the sex life is blocked, the writer tends to become irritable, quarrelsome or contentious.

This exposes anxiety in intimate relationships. The writers tend to be impatient, nagging and aggressive.
See listing 15-4b on page 150.
See listing 31-8 on page 180.
See listing 15-b on page 93.
See listing 27-7a on page 155.

indikator.nama: Upper zone loops with angular apexes
indikator.keterangan:
The writer suffers from undefined inner feelings of dread that he is unable to explain. He cannot understand his anxiety nor can he control his response to it. The apprehension is chronic and illogical, although the writer may be logical otherwise.

The writer has difficulty making decisions. Enthusiasm and optimism are both low.

indikator.nama: Alignment with words sinking at the end of the line
indikator.keterangan:
Words sinking at the end of the line are not related to negativism. They are evidence of poor organizational ability.

The writer has poor planning ability. He misjudges time and materials necessary to complete a job. Initially, he tends to be extravagant and wasteful with both. When he realizes that he cannot finish a project in the allotted time, he tries to complete too much work at the last minute with too few resources.
See listing 26-2a on page 148.

indikator.nama: Letters or parts of letters or words missing
indikator.keterangan: See listing 36-2b on page 216.

indikator.nama: Last part of one letter is first part of following letter
indikator.keterangan: See listing 39-5b on page 235.
See listing 33-6b on page 195.
The writer lacks mental discipline. He has lofty ideas but often confuses facts with fantasies. He does not have the persistence and self-directive ability to turn his flights of fancy into reality.
See listing 36-3 on page 216.

indikator.nama: Lower zone loops entangle with middle zone of following line
indikator.keterangan: See listing 29-4b on page 165.
See listing 03-5 on page 17.
See listing 36-6b on page 218.

The writer needs an exorbitant amount of self-praise to fulfill his ego needs. He wants power to compensate for feelings of inadequacy. He dislikes having to do things that are “unworthy” of him.

The writer lacks mental control. It is hard for him to communicate logically or to concentrate for any length of time. He is unable to judge matters realistically and is often confused about facts. His biggest problem is his lack of information. He feels he has nothing to learn because he already knows it all. He refuses advice, even if others make repeated efforts to make him listen. He looks at most people as incompetents and assumes that he can do anything better than they can. He feels free to step in and start arranging their lives and their projects. If he fails, he either blames other people or tries to convince himself and others of the illusion of success.

The writer presumes too much. He thinks himself superior to others and feels he can get away with things other people would get penalized for. He feels alone most of the time because his superior attitude shuts others out.
See listing 27-8a on page 156.

indikator.nama: Score for Anxiety (# 39) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan: The writer experiences feelings of dread and apprehension without specific cause. He suffers from frequent distractions and momentarily forgets what he was thinking about. He may be prone to making errors.

indikator.nama: Score for Tension (# 30) is 5.0 or higher
indikator.keterangan:
The writer suffers from feelings of inner strain, accompanied by discomfort and apprehension. He feels constantly driven and under pressure. He is prone to overreact to minor annoyances and finds it hard to stay composed.

His reasoning ability is impaired. His thoughts tend so scatter and that makes it difficult for him to concentrate. While he works adequately at familiar tasks, he has difficulty dealing with unfamiliar or demanding jobs.
